中国外交部对美国尖端半导体出口新规作出反弹

针对美国商务部公布尖端半导体等出口新规一事，中国外交部发言人11月17日在记者会上作出反弹，表示今后将采取必要措施。

在美国有报道称，英伟达的尖端半导体可能通过第三国绕道出口到了美国政府的出口管制对象国中国。

在此背景下，美国商务部16日公布了有关尖端半导体等产品的出口新规。根据新规定，今后在向印度尼西亚、马来西亚、新加坡、泰国和巴西的企业出口尖端半导体时，必须事先获得许可。因为美国政府认为半导体产品通过这些国家绕道出口至中国等国的风险较大。

对此，中国外交部发言人郭嘉昆在17日的记者会上说，“美方滥用出口管制措施，甚至横加干涉中国同其他国家开展正常贸易与科技合作，无理打压中国高新技术产业发展”。

在此之上，他还表示，美方举动“损害中国企业正当权益，扰乱全球产供链稳定。中方将采取必要措施坚决维护自身正当权益”。

KATIE ROGERS, DAVID E. SANGER2026年11月18日

特朗普总统周二抵达马尼拉，开启为期48小时的亚洲之行。 Doug Mills/The New York Times

President Trump arrived in Manila on Tuesday, at the tail end of a diplomatic summit in which world leaders had arranged to hold part of the gathering at his hotel. His agenda was supposed to be about inking trade deals and embracing regional partnerships, but several problems from home had followed him overseas.

特朗普总统周二抵达马尼拉，当时一场外交峰会已接近尾声，世界各国领导人此前已安排在他下榻的酒店举行部分会议。他的行程本应围绕签署贸易协议和推进区域伙伴关系展开，但国内的几个问题却随他到了海外。

He was pelted with questions. He seemed to meet each with a shrug.

他面对一连串的提问。他似乎对每一个问题都耸耸肩予以回应。

Did he have any worries about the aviation-system meltdown afflicting travelers across the United States, or a technological outage affecting several large banking systems?

他是否担忧正在困扰全美旅客的航空系统瘫痪、或是影响多家大型银行系统的技术故障？

“It’s life,” Mr. Trump said. “When you’re big and powerful and you have all the money, things like that happen. It’s fine.”

“这就是生活，”特朗普说。“当你强大且富有，拥有大量金钱，就会发生这种事。这没关系。”

Mr. Trump is not shy about prizing photo opportunities. But his appearance showcased just how little he seemed to be interested in netting diplomatic wins or easing concerns about American leadership — his leadership — as he made this quick stop at the Association of Southeast Asian Nations.

特朗普向来不吝于利用拍照机会。但他的露面表明，在东南亚国家联盟进行短暂逗留时，他似乎既无意争取外交成果，也无意缓解外界对美国领导力——也就是他本人领导力——的担忧。

His appearance was on the way to the main event later in the week: a meeting on the edges of the APEC economic summit in Shenzhen, China, on Thursday with Presidents Xi Jinping of China and Vladimir V. Putin of Russia, two authoritarians whom Mr. Trump openly admires.

这次露面是他此行的途中一站，重头戏则是本周晚些时候：周四在中国深圳举行的亚太经合组织经济峰会期间，他将与中国国家主席习近平和俄罗斯总统普京举行会晤，这两位威权领导人都是特朗普公开推崇的。

Mr. Trump will be meeting Mr. Xi for the third time this year, and there is another likely next month at Mr. Trump’s Doral resort in Miami, where he gets to play the host (and has invited Mr. Putin, ending the Russian leader’s isolation for invading Ukraine). The three-way meeting between China, Russia and the United States would be the first of its kind.

这将是特朗普今年第三次会见习近平，下个月两人可能会在特朗普位于迈阿密的多拉度假村举行另一次会晤，届时他是东道主（他还邀请了普京，结束了这位俄罗斯领导人因入侵乌克兰而受到的孤立）。这样的中俄美三方会晤将是史无前例的。

Mr. Trump’s visit to Manila amounted to a layover. When he arrived, he trudged off the plane like all weary long-haul travelers do, and slowly made his way down the stairs of Air Force One. Mr. Trump was then whisked to his hotel, where several world leaders had gathered to bring the diplomatic summit to his doorstep.

特朗普对马尼拉的访问相当于一次中转。抵达时，他像所有疲惫的长途旅客一样步履沉重地走出飞机，慢慢地走下“空军一号”的舷梯。随后特朗普被迅速送往他下榻的酒店，几位世界领导人聚集在那里，将外交峰会带到了他的门口。

周二在马尼拉举行的东盟-美国峰会上，从左至右依次为：日本首相高市早苗、印度总理纳伦德拉·莫迪、特朗普和澳大利亚总理安东尼·阿尔巴内塞。

Alongside members of the so-called Quad — the informal grouping that includes the United States, India, Japan and Australia — his comments were brief, cryptic and nearly mechanical: “Quad is important. We’re working on things that will surprise people.”

在与“四方安全对话”（Quad，包括美国、印度、日本和澳大利亚在内的非正式机制）成员会面时，他的发言简短、隐晦且几乎是机械式的：“Quad很重要。我们正在做一些会让人感到惊讶的事情。”

On the way to Manila, Mr. Trump floated a meeting with another leader, Kim Jong Un, the North Korean leader and a dictator he has talked warmly about, perhaps in Shenzhen. It isn’t clear why he wants to see Mr. Kim: The three meetings he held in his first term ended in failure, and today the North has more nuclear weapons, and more ways to launch them, than ever before.

前往马尼拉途中，特朗普提出可能会与另一位领导人——朝鲜领导人金正恩会面，也许就在深圳。他曾热情地谈论过这位独裁者。目前尚不清楚他为什么要见金正恩：他在第一任期内与金正恩举行的三次会晤均以失败告终，而朝鲜如今拥有比以往任何时候都多的核武器，以及更多发射核武器的方式。

If he holds the meeting it would also surprise his staff. Last week, White House officials said that there was no chance of a Trump-Kim meeting. On Tuesday, the White House did not explain whether plans for such a meeting were taking shape.

如果他举行这次会晤，他的幕僚都会感到惊讶。上周，白宫官员表示特朗普与金正恩没有会面的可能。周二，白宫没有解释举行此类会晤的计划是否正在成型。

During an address to Quad leaders on Tuesday evening, Mr. Trump again focused on personal relationships over policy. He called Prime Minister Narendra Modi of India, a member of the group, “a great leader and a friend of mine, highly respected by everybody all over the world.” The president also praised Mr. Modi as a “very tough man.” The countries are at odds over India’s purchases of Russian oil, and trade talks have dragged on, frustrating both parties.

在周二晚上向四方机制领导人发表讲话时，特朗普再次将重点放在了个人关系而非政策上。他称该组织成员、印度总理纳伦德拉·莫迪是“一位伟大的领导人和我的朋友，受到全世界所有人的高度尊重”。总统还称赞莫迪是一个“非常强硬的人”。美印两国因印度购买俄罗斯石油而产生分歧，贸易谈判被拖延，这让双方都感到沮丧。

Later, the Quad leaders issued a joint statement, affirming the group as “a force for good and a partnership of action, committed to peace, stability, and prosperity” and outlining several plans, including maritime flyovers of the Indo-Pacific, cooperation on combating cyberattacks, and accelerating work on A.I. initiatives.

随后，四方机制领导人发表了一份联合声明，肯定该机制是“一股向善的力量和行动的伙伴关系，致力于和平、稳定与繁荣”，并概述了多项计划，包括印太地区的海上飞越、在打击网络攻击方面的合作以及加速人工智能倡议的工作。

Before ending his day, Mr. Trump delivered remarks at a dinner of ASEAN leaders, and praised his host, President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. of the Philippines.

在结束一天的行程之前，特朗普在东盟领导人晚宴上发表了讲话，并赞扬了东道主菲律宾总统小费迪南德·马科斯。

“I don’t want to date myself, but I knew your parents very well. They were great,” Mr. Trump said. “I believe in genetics. They did a good job. You have very good genetics, I can tell you that.”

“我不想暴露我的年龄，但我非常了解你的父母。他们很伟大，”特朗普说。“我相信遗传。他们做得很好。你拥有非常好的基因，我可以告诉你这一点。”

特朗普与泰国总理阿努廷·查恩维拉库尔出席了签字仪式，但特朗普表示贸易协议尚未最终敲定。

It was not the first time Mr. Trump has praised the family of Mr. Marcos, who is the son of the dictator Ferdinand E. Marcos, who ruled the Philippines for 20 years, imposed martial law, and was ousted in 1986.

这不是特朗普第一次赞扬马科斯家族。小马科斯是独裁者费迪南德·马科斯的儿子，老马科斯曾统治菲律宾20年，实施戒严令，并于1986年被推翻。

On Wednesday, Mr. Trump will stay in Manila long enough to have lunch at Malacañang Palace and a bilateral meeting with Mr. Marcos before departing for Shenzhen.

周三，特朗普将在马尼拉停留足够长的时间，在马拉卡南宫吃午餐并与马科斯举行双边会晤，然后启程前往深圳。

In China, Mr. Trump needs to extend a soon-expiring trade truce that limited tariffs on Chinese goods entering the United States in return for a Chinese commitment not to cut off rare earths and magnets.

在中国，特朗普需要延长一项即将到期的贸易休战协议，该协议限制了进入美国的中国商品的关税，以换取中国不切断稀土和磁铁供应的承诺。

The president is also going to focus on the issue of nuclear proliferation in his meeting with Mr. Xi and Mr. Putin, though White House officials do not expect any significant breakthroughs.

总统在与习近平和普京的会晤中也将聚焦核扩散问题，尽管白宫官员并不期待取得任何重大突破。

Also lingering over Mr. Trump’s trip to Asia is the fallout from the resignation of Jensen Huang, the chief executive of the chip maker Nvidia, after revelations he had engaged in extramarital affairs, including with a woman whom U.S. officials have identified as a Chinese intelligence asset.

黄仁勋在塑造总统对华技术竞争观点方面一直具有影响力，他认为，让中国依赖美国制造的半导体芯片和技术有助于维持美国对北京的主导地位。

Mr. Huang has been influential in shaping the president’s views about technological competition with China, and made the argument that keeping China dependent on American-made semiconductor chips and technology could help maintain U.S. dominance over Beijing.

黄仁勋的辞职以及商务部在放缓旨在限制向海外数据中心销售英伟达芯片的规定方面所采取的做法暴露了特朗普政府内部由来已久的矛盾。商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克和财政部长斯科特·贝森特陪同特朗普出访，卢特尼克主张对亚洲芯片出口实施较宽松限制，贝森特则在近日公开指责商务部未能限制先进的英伟达技术的销售。

特朗普在东盟领导人晚宴上发表讲话。晚宴期间，他谈到了菲律宾总统费迪南德·马科斯二世的家人。

Mr. Huang’s resignation — and the approach the Commerce Department took to slowing rules that would clamp down on the sale of Nvidia chips to overseas data centers — has exposed a long-burning feud within the Trump administration. Howard Lutnick, the commerce secretary, who has argued for less strict limits on chip exports to Asia, joined Mr. Trump for the trip, as did Scott Bessent, the Treasury secretary, who in recent days publicly blamed the Commerce Department for failing to clamp down on the sale of advanced Nvidia technology.

启程前往马尼拉之前，特朗普似乎并不担心这桩震动了对人工智能行业至关重要的企业巨头的丑闻。当被问及间谍活动时，他通常的反驳是所有人都在这么做，他似乎并没有特别感到不安。如果他确实感到不安，他也不会表现出来。

Before leaving for Manila, Mr. Trump did not seem concerned about the scandal that has rocked a corporate juggernaut that is critical to the A.I. industry. His usual retort when asked about spying is that everyone does it, and he did not seem especially perturbed. If he was, he would not show it.

“你知道，我们要去中国，我认为你不会想在到达中国之前就侮辱中国，”特朗普说。

Verena Hölzl和Suhasini Raj对本文有报道贡献。

Katie Rogers是《纽约时报》白宫记者，报道特朗普总统相关新闻。

David E. Sanger报道特朗普政府和一系列国家安全问题。他在时报任职超过40年，著有四本关于美国国家安全挑战的书。

随后，四方机制领导人发表了一份联合声明，肯定该机制是“一股向善的力量和行动的伙伴关系，致力于和平、稳定与繁荣”，并概述了多项计划，包括印太地区的海上飞越、在打击网络攻击方面的合作以及加速人工智能倡议的工作。
Before ending his day, Mr. Trump delivered remarks at a dinner of ASEAN leaders, and praised his host, President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. of the Philippines.
在结束一天的行程之前，特朗普在东盟领导人晚宴上发表了讲话，并赞扬了东道主菲律宾总统小费迪南德·马科斯。
“I don’t want to date myself, but I knew your parents very well. They were great,” Mr. Trump said. “I believe in genetics. They did a good job. You have very good genetics, I can tell you that.”
“我不想暴露我的年龄，但我非常了解你的父母。他们很伟大，”特朗普说。“我相信遗传。他们做得很好。你拥有非常好的基因，我可以告诉你这一点。”
特朗普与泰国总理阿努廷·查恩维拉库尔出席了签字仪式，但特朗普表示贸易协议尚未最终敲定。

It was not the first time Mr. Trump has praised the family of Mr. Marcos, who is the son of the dictator Ferdinand E. Marcos, who ruled the Philippines for 20 years, imposed martial law, and was ousted in 1986.
这不是特朗普第一次赞扬马科斯家族。小马科斯是独裁者费迪南德·马科斯的儿子，老马科斯曾统治菲律宾20年，实施戒严令，并于1986年被推翻。
On Wednesday, Mr. Trump will stay in Manila long enough to have lunch at Malacañang Palace and a bilateral meeting with Mr. Marcos before departing for Shenzhen.
周三，特朗普将在马尼拉停留足够长的时间，在马拉卡南宫吃午餐并与马科斯举行双边会晤，然后启程前往深圳。

In China, Mr. Trump needs to extend a soon-expiring trade truce that limited tariffs on Chinese goods entering the United States in return for a Chinese commitment not to cut off rare earths and magnets.
在中国，特朗普需要延长一项即将到期的贸易休战协议，该协议限制了进入美国的中国商品的关税，以换取中国不切断稀土和磁铁供应的承诺。
The president is also going to focus on the issue of nuclear proliferation in his meeting with Mr. Xi and Mr. Putin, though White House officials do not expect any significant breakthroughs.
总统在与习近平和普京的会晤中也将聚焦核扩散问题，尽管白宫官员并不期待取得任何重大突破。

Also lingering over Mr. Trump’s trip to Asia is the fallout from the resignation of Jensen Huang, the chief executive of the chip maker Nvidia, after revelations he had engaged in extramarital affairs, including with a woman whom U.S. officials have identified as a Chinese intelligence asset.
黄仁勋在塑造总统对华技术竞争观点方面一直具有影响力，他认为，让中国依赖美国制造的半导体芯片和技术有助于维持美国对北京的主导地位。

Mr. Huang has been influential in shaping the president’s views about technological competition with China, and made the argument that keeping China dependent on American-made semiconductor chips and technology could help maintain U.S. dominance over Beijing.
黄仁勋的辞职以及商务部在放缓旨在限制向海外数据中心销售英伟达芯片的规定方面所采取的做法暴露了特朗普政府内部由来已久的矛盾。商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克和财政部长斯科特·贝森特陪同特朗普出访，卢特尼克主张对亚洲芯片出口实施较宽松限制，贝森特则在近日公开指责商务部未能限制先进的英伟达技术的销售。
特朗普在东盟领导人晚宴上发表讲话。晚宴期间，他谈到了菲律宾总统费迪南德·马科斯二世的家人。

Mr. Huang’s resignation — and the approach the Commerce Department took to slowing rules that would clamp down on the sale of Nvidia chips to overseas data centers — has exposed a long-burning feud within the Trump administration. Howard Lutnick, the commerce secretary, who has argued for less strict limits on chip exports to Asia, joined Mr. Trump for the trip, as did Scott Bessent, the Treasury secretary, who in recent days publicly blamed the Commerce Department for failing to clamp down on the sale of advanced Nvidia technology.
启程前往马尼拉之前，特朗普似乎并不担心这桩震动了对人工智能行业至关重要的企业巨头的丑闻。当被问及间谍活动时，他通常的反驳是所有人都在这么做，他似乎并没有特别感到不安。如果他确实感到不安，他也不会表现出来。

Before leaving for Manila, Mr. Trump did not seem concerned about the scandal that has rocked a corporate juggernaut that is critical to the A.I. industry. His usual retort when asked about spying is that everyone does it, and he did not seem especially perturbed. If he was, he would not show it.
“你知道，我们要去中国，我认为你不会想在到达中国之前就侮辱中国，”特朗普说。
Verena Hölzl和Suhasini Raj对本文有报道贡献。
Katie Rogers是《纽约时报》白宫记者，报道特朗普总统相关新闻。
David E. Sanger报道特朗普政府和一系列国家安全问题。他在时报任职超过40年，著有四本关于美国国家安全挑战的书。

items.body:
DAVID PIERSON2026年11月18日

中国领导人习近平周二在中国深圳出席一场会议。通过在这个科技中心主办亚太经合组织峰会，习近平可能希望借此证明中国的增长可以惠及世界。 Pool photo by Maxim Shemetov

When China’s then-paramount leader, Deng Xiaoping, toured Shenzhen in 1992, he used the southern Chinese city to signal an embrace of open markets, setting off decades of rapid growth that would make his country the world’s factory floor.

1992年时任中国最高领导人邓小平视察深圳时，他利用这座中国南方城市释放了拥抱开放市场的信号，开启了数十年的快速增长，最终使他的国家成为了世界工厂。

Since then, Shenzhen has grown from a sleepy town into a gleaming metropolis that dwarfs its more established neighbor, Hong Kong. Apple’s main assembler, Foxconn, runs a sprawling campus there, and Walmart manages its China business from the city. It is home to many Chinese brands like Huawei, BYD and the drone maker DJI.

自那时起，深圳从一个偏僻小镇发展成为闪耀的大都市，甚至令早已声名显赫的邻居香港相形见绌。苹果的主要组装商富士康在这里运营着一个庞大的园区，沃尔玛在此管理其中国业务。它也是华为、比亚迪和无人机制造商大疆等众多中国品牌的总部所在地。

This week, China’s leader, Xi Jinping, is hosting a regional economic summit in the same city, using it to make the case that China’s growth can benefit the world. Shenzhen has been primped for the occasion, with bus shelters plastered with the slogan: “Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together.”

本周，中国领导人习近平在这座城市主办一场区域经济峰会，以此来证明中国的增长可以惠及世界。深圳已为此场合进行了精心布置，公交候车亭贴满了标语：“建设亚太共同体，促进共同繁荣。”

But some of that message may be difficult to square for many of China’s trading partners. To them, Shenzhen also embodies much of what makes the world uneasy about China today: a flood of cheap exports; tech giants that pose security risks; and a Communist Party that has traded Mr. Deng’s freewheeling experimentation for more state control.

但对于中国的许多贸易伙伴来说，其中一些信息可能难以接受。对他们而言，深圳也同样体现了当今世界对中国感到不安的诸多因素：廉价出口商品的泛滥、构成安全风险的科技巨头，以及一个用更多的国家控制取代了邓小平的自由试验的共产党。

Mr. Xi’s moment in the spotlight at the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation forum will also be clouded by allegations of a Chinese spy scandal at the American chip giant, Nvidia, that has already prompted Washington to tighten Chinese access to advanced American chips.

习近平在亚太经合组织论坛上备受瞩目的时刻也将因美国芯片巨头英伟达的中国间谍丑闻指控蒙上阴影，该指控已经促使华盛顿收紧中国获取先进美国芯片的渠道。

And he is set to meet for the first time with President Trump and President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia, a gathering that could unsettle smaller powers like Ukraine. (Mr. Trump has also suggested that he might see the North Korean dictator Kim Jong-un while in China.)

他将首次与特朗普总统和俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·V·普京举行会晤，这次聚会可能会让乌克兰等小国感到不安。（特朗普也曾暗示，他在中国期间可能会与朝鲜独裁者金正恩见面。）

Here’s what is on China’s agenda when Mr. Xi takes center stage in Shenzhen:

以下是习近平在深圳登上舞台中心时中国方面的议程：

Showcase of China’s Tech Ambitions

展示中国的科技雄心

In some ways, the setting itself could be read as a statement of defiance.

从某种意义上说，选择深圳作为举办地本身就可以被解读为一种反抗的声明。

Shenzhen is home to companies Washington has labeled national security risks, like Huawei and ZTE, as well as Chinese artificial intelligence labs racing to close the gap with American rivals. Many of the companies have been subjected to American sanctions and blacklists.

深圳是华为、中兴等被华盛顿贴上国家安全风险标签的公司的总部，也是许多中国人工智能实验室的所在地，这些实验室正竞相缩小与美国竞争对手的差距。许多公司都受到了美国的制裁并被列入黑名单。

Mr. Xi wants to show that “China can do well despite America’s all-out effort to kill it” with those trade restrictions, said Minxin Pei, a professor at Claremont McKenna College who studies Chinese leadership politics.

研究中国领导层政治的克莱蒙特·麦肯纳学院教授裴敏欣表示，习近平希望表明，尽管美国竭尽全力通过这些贸易限制手段进行打压，但“中国依然可以发展得很好”。

深圳的一家华为门店。这家公司已被美国政府贴上国家安全风险的标签。

That is an image that Beijing has tried to cultivate after Washington began restricting direct sales of advanced chips to China in 2022, pointing to Huawei’s homegrown processors and DeepSeek’s and other Chinese labs’ breakthrough A.I. models as proof that U.S. restrictions have failed.

自华盛顿于2022年开始限制向中国直接销售先进芯片以来，北京一直试图树立这种形象，将华为的国产处理器以及DeepSeek等中国实验室的突破性人工智能模型作为美国限制措施没有见效的证明。

Beijing is also casting itself as a partner to other countries in technological advancement, offering Chinese cooperation and know-how on A.I., an approach that competes with the United States’ attempts to unite partners around A.I. supply chains independent of China.

北京还将自己塑造成其他国家在技术进步方面的合作伙伴，提供中国在人工智能方面的合作和专业知识，抗衡美国试图团结合作伙伴、建立不依赖中国的人工智能供应链的策略。

What Espionage?

哪有什么间谍活动？

For China, the news had threatened to distract from the upcoming summit. Less than three weeks before the gathering, The New York Times reported that a Chinese businesswoman who had a close relationship with Jensen Huang, the chief executive of Nvidia, was found to be passing intelligence to Beijing. In the days since, Mr. Huang has stepped down and the company’s board has said it would conduct an investigation.

对中国而言，近期的新闻可能会转移人们对即将召开的峰会的注意力。在距离会议还不到三周的时候，《纽约时报》报道称，一名与英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋关系密切的中国女商人被发现向北京传递情报。此后的几天里，黄仁勋已经辞职，公司董事会表示将展开调查。

The allegations, which China has denied, could have scuttled talks with Mr. Trump and put the countries’ fragile trade truce at risk. The claim of such a bold espionage plot was also a potential source of embarrassment for a country hosting business and government leaders at a major event.

这些被中国否认的指控原本可能会破坏与特朗普的会谈，并危及两国脆弱的贸易休战。对于一个要在重要活动中接待商界和政府领导人的国家来说，如此直白的间谍阴谋指控可能也会引起尴尬。

3月，英伟达前首席执行官黄仁勋。《纽约时报》报道称，一名与黄仁勋关系密切的中国女商人被发现向北京传递情报。

China has carried on as if it were business as usual. And in a way, Beijing has already scored a win: The controversy has failed to derail the scheduled talks between Mr. Xi and Mr. Trump, who has downplayed the alleged spy plot.

中国在继续推进议程，仿佛什么都没有发生。在某种程度上，北京已经取得了一场胜利：这一争议未能破坏习近平与特朗普之间的预定会谈，特朗普已经淡化了被指存在的间谍阴谋。

Rather than declaring that he would confront China about the Nvidia scandal, Mr. Trump has said he does not intend to bring it up. “I don’t think you want to insult China just before you get there,” he told reporters outside the White House on Monday when asked about divisions within his administration about how tough to be on China.

特朗普并未宣布他将就英伟达丑闻与中国对抗，而是表示他不打算提及此事。周一，当在白宫外被问及其政府内部在对华强硬程度上的分歧时，他告诉记者：“我认为你不应该在去中国之前去得罪它。”

But the scandal is already costing China. On Monday, the Trump administration issued a rule to stop Chinese companies from accessing advanced Nvidia chips through data centers in third countries, and to require licenses for chip exports to companies in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil.

但这项丑闻已经让中国付出了代价。周一，特朗普政府发布了一项规定，阻止中国公司通过第三国的数据中心获取先进的英伟达芯片，并要求向马来西亚、新加坡、泰国、印度尼西亚和巴西的公司出口芯片必须获得许可。

China Needs to Ease Trade Concerns

中国需要缓解贸易担忧

China’s export machinery is practically unbeatable. This month, China reported that its exports exceeded its imports by more than $1 trillion in the first 10 months of this year, putting it on track to eclipse last year’s record.

中国的出口机器几乎不可战胜。中国本月报告称，今年前10个月贸易顺差超过1万亿美元，有望打破去年的纪录。

But as its factories have churned out solar panels, electric cars and other goods for consumers globally, China has faced pushback not only from the United States but from around the world. It needs to head off efforts by trading partners like the European Union to block its exports.

但随着中国工厂大量生产太阳能电池板、电动汽车和其他面向全球消费者的商品，中国不仅面临来自美国的抵制，还面临来自世界各地的抵制。它需要阻止欧盟等贸易伙伴阻碍其出口的努力。

That’s why China is billing the event as an opportunity for the region to champion free trade and oppose protectionism.

这就是为什么中国将此次活动宣传为该地区倡导自由贸易和反对保护主义的一个机会。

去年，中国合肥一家汽车工厂生产线上工作的员工。北京一直力推国产品牌、挤压外资品牌市场。

In reality, China has been turning inward. Beijing has sought to squeeze out foreign technology, electronics and auto brands in favor of Chinese firms. The Communist Party, which under Mr. Xi has tightened its grip on the economy, vowed last month to expand its presence inside internet companies. Shen Weizhong, a former policy planner with China’s Foreign Ministry, called the approach “manageable openness,” in which security weighs as heavily as growth.

实际上，中国一直在转向内向型发展。北京试图挤压外国技术、电子产品和汽车品牌的市场，扶持中国企业。在习近平领导下加强了对经济控制的共产党上个月誓言要扩大其在互联网公司内部的影响力。前中国外交部政策规划官员沈伟中称这种做法是“可控的开放”，其中安全与增长同等重要。

Mr. Xi’s willingness to turn the world’s dependence on Chinese goods into leverage has also alienated other countries.

习近平意在将世界对中国商品的依赖转化为筹码，这也疏远了其他国家。

Beijing imposed controls on exports of rare earths last year, and it has recently moved to restrict the exports of dozens of technologies, including drones, artificial intelligence models and agents, and know-how about advanced medicines and solar panels. China says these measures are a response to U.S. blacklists and export restrictions.

北京去年对稀土出口实施了管制，最近又采取行动限制数十项技术的出口，包括无人机、人工智能模型和智能体，以及有关先进药物和太阳能电池板的专业知识。中国表示，这些措施是对美国黑名单和出口限制的回应。

“Chinese leaders recognize that the golden era of globalization is over, and geoeconomic competition has become the new normal,” said Yuen Yuen Ang, a professor of political economy at Johns Hopkins University.

“中国领导人认识到，全球化的黄金时代已经结束，地缘经济竞争已成为新常态，”约翰斯·霍普金斯大学政治经济学教授洪源远表示。

Putin, Trump … and Kim?

普京、特朗普……还有金正恩？

Mr. Xi is expected to sit down with Mr. Trump and Mr. Putin on Thursday, a meeting that is without precedent. China’s Foreign Ministry on Monday called the meeting one “of groundbreaking significance.”

预计习近平将于周四与特朗普和普京举行会谈，这是一次史无前例的会议。中国外交部周一称这次会议“具有开创性意义”。

For Beijing, the gathering casts China as a power broker that can bring Washington and Moscow to the same table. Mr. Xi wants to show the world, and especially his own people, that China under his leadership is “consequential, influential and highly respected, with enormous convening power,” said Mr. Pei of Claremont McKenna.

对北京来说，这次聚会将中国塑造成一个能够让华盛顿和莫斯科坐到同一张谈判桌前的权力中间人。克莱蒙特·麦肯纳学院的裴敏欣表示，习近平希望向世界、特别是向本国人民展示，在他领导下的中国是“举足轻重、有影响力且备受尊重的，拥有巨大的号召力”。

But the optics are awkward.

但舆论观感有些尴尬。

5月，习近平与俄罗斯总统普京在北京。预计这两位领导人将在深圳与特朗普举行会谈，这将是一次史无前例的会议。

Mr. Trump said on Monday that he planned to discuss the war in Ukraine in Shenzhen. Beijing is reluctant to take the lead on peace talks, said Zhao Long, a senior research fellow at the Shanghai Institutes for International Studies, lest it create “the wrong impression” that “major powers are dividing up the interests of other countries.”

特朗普周一表示，他计划在深圳讨论乌克兰战争。上海国际问题研究院高级研究员赵隆表示，北京不愿在和平谈判中牵头，以免造成“大国正在瓜分其他国家利益”的“错误印象”。

And Mr. Trump has raised the possibility of another guest: the North Korean dictator, Kim Jong-un. He told reporters on Monday as he left the White House: “And we may meet with Kim Jong Un, also. So, that’ll be good. We could — we have a chance to accomplish a lot.”

特朗普还提出了另一位客人的可能性：朝鲜独裁者金正恩。他周一离开白宫时告诉记者：“我们可能还会见金正恩。所以，那会很好。我们可以——我们有机会取得很多成就。”

A spokesman for China’s foreign ministry, Guo Jiakun, asked on Tuesday if Mr. Kim would be attending, said: “I do not have information on this.” Russian state news agencies reported that Mr. Putin could meet with Mr. Kim if the North Korean leader travels to China, citing Dmitri S. Peskov, the Kremlin’s spokesman.

中国外交部发言人郭嘉昆周二在被问及金正恩是否会出席时表示：“我们没有这方面的信息。”俄罗斯国家通讯社援引克里姆林宫发言人德米特里·S·佩斯科夫的话报道称，如果这位朝鲜领导人前往中国，普京可能会与他会面。

Berry Wang、Keith Bradsher、Ruoxin Zhang和Siyi Zhao对本文有报道和研究贡献。

David Pierson报道中国外交政策和中国与世界的经济与文化交互。他从事新闻工作已超过20年。

中国领导人习近平周二在中国深圳出席一场会议。通过在这个科技中心主办亚太经合组织峰会，习近平可能希望借此证明中国的增长可以惠及世界。 Pool photo by Maxim Shemetov

When China’s then-paramount leader, Deng Xiaoping, toured Shenzhen in 1992, he used the southern Chinese city to signal an embrace of open markets, setting off decades of rapid growth that would make his country the world’s factory floor.
1992年时任中国最高领导人邓小平视察深圳时，他利用这座中国南方城市释放了拥抱开放市场的信号，开启了数十年的快速增长，最终使他的国家成为了世界工厂。

Since then, Shenzhen has grown from a sleepy town into a gleaming metropolis that dwarfs its more established neighbor, Hong Kong. Apple’s main assembler, Foxconn, runs a sprawling campus there, and Walmart manages its China business from the city. It is home to many Chinese brands like Huawei, BYD and the drone maker DJI.
自那时起，深圳从一个偏僻小镇发展成为闪耀的大都市，甚至令早已声名显赫的邻居香港相形见绌。苹果的主要组装商富士康在这里运营着一个庞大的园区，沃尔玛在此管理其中国业务。它也是华为、比亚迪和无人机制造商大疆等众多中国品牌的总部所在地。

This week, China’s leader, Xi Jinping, is hosting a regional economic summit in the same city, using it to make the case that China’s growth can benefit the world. Shenzhen has been primped for the occasion, with bus shelters plastered with the slogan: “Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together.”
本周，中国领导人习近平在这座城市主办一场区域经济峰会，以此来证明中国的增长可以惠及世界。深圳已为此场合进行了精心布置，公交候车亭贴满了标语：“建设亚太共同体，促进共同繁荣。”

But some of that message may be difficult to square for many of China’s trading partners. To them, Shenzhen also embodies much of what makes the world uneasy about China today: a flood of cheap exports; tech giants that pose security risks; and a Communist Party that has traded Mr. Deng’s freewheeling experimentation for more state control.
但对于中国的许多贸易伙伴来说，其中一些信息可能难以接受。对他们而言，深圳也同样体现了当今世界对中国感到不安的诸多因素：廉价出口商品的泛滥、构成安全风险的科技巨头，以及一个用更多的国家控制取代了邓小平的自由试验的共产党。

Mr. Xi’s moment in the spotlight at the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation forum will also be clouded by allegations of a Chinese spy scandal at the American chip giant, Nvidia, that has already prompted Washington to tighten Chinese access to advanced American chips.
习近平在亚太经合组织论坛上备受瞩目的时刻也将因美国芯片巨头英伟达的中国间谍丑闻指控蒙上阴影，该指控已经促使华盛顿收紧中国获取先进美国芯片的渠道。

And he is set to meet for the first time with President Trump and President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia, a gathering that could unsettle smaller powers like Ukraine. (Mr. Trump has also suggested that he might see the North Korean dictator Kim Jong-un while in China.)
他将首次与特朗普总统和俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·V·普京举行会晤，这次聚会可能会让乌克兰等小国感到不安。（特朗普也曾暗示，他在中国期间可能会与朝鲜独裁者金正恩见面。）
Here’s what is on China’s agenda when Mr. Xi takes center stage in Shenzhen:
以下是习近平在深圳登上舞台中心时中国方面的议程：
Showcase of China’s Tech Ambitions
展示中国的科技雄心
In some ways, the setting itself could be read as a statement of defiance.
从某种意义上说，选择深圳作为举办地本身就可以被解读为一种反抗的声明。

Shenzhen is home to companies Washington has labeled national security risks, like Huawei and ZTE, as well as Chinese artificial intelligence labs racing to close the gap with American rivals. Many of the companies have been subjected to American sanctions and blacklists.
深圳是华为、中兴等被华盛顿贴上国家安全风险标签的公司的总部，也是许多中国人工智能实验室的所在地，这些实验室正竞相缩小与美国竞争对手的差距。许多公司都受到了美国的制裁并被列入黑名单。

Mr. Xi wants to show that “China can do well despite America’s all-out effort to kill it” with those trade restrictions, said Minxin Pei, a professor at Claremont McKenna College who studies Chinese leadership politics.
研究中国领导层政治的克莱蒙特·麦肯纳学院教授裴敏欣表示，习近平希望表明，尽管美国竭尽全力通过这些贸易限制手段进行打压，但“中国依然可以发展得很好”。
深圳的一家华为门店。这家公司已被美国政府贴上国家安全风险的标签。

That is an image that Beijing has tried to cultivate after Washington began restricting direct sales of advanced chips to China in 2022, pointing to Huawei’s homegrown processors and DeepSeek’s and other Chinese labs’ breakthrough A.I. models as proof that U.S. restrictions have failed.
自华盛顿于2022年开始限制向中国直接销售先进芯片以来，北京一直试图树立这种形象，将华为的国产处理器以及DeepSeek等中国实验室的突破性人工智能模型作为美国限制措施没有见效的证明。

Beijing is also casting itself as a partner to other countries in technological advancement, offering Chinese cooperation and know-how on A.I., an approach that competes with the United States’ attempts to unite partners around A.I. supply chains independent of China.
北京还将自己塑造成其他国家在技术进步方面的合作伙伴，提供中国在人工智能方面的合作和专业知识，抗衡美国试图团结合作伙伴、建立不依赖中国的人工智能供应链的策略。
What Espionage?
哪有什么间谍活动？

For China, the news had threatened to distract from the upcoming summit. Less than three weeks before the gathering, The New York Times reported that a Chinese businesswoman who had a close relationship with Jensen Huang, the chief executive of Nvidia, was found to be passing intelligence to Beijing. In the days since, Mr. Huang has stepped down and the company’s board has said it would conduct an investigation.
对中国而言，近期的新闻可能会转移人们对即将召开的峰会的注意力。在距离会议还不到三周的时候，《纽约时报》报道称，一名与英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋关系密切的中国女商人被发现向北京传递情报。此后的几天里，黄仁勋已经辞职，公司董事会表示将展开调查。

The allegations, which China has denied, could have scuttled talks with Mr. Trump and put the countries’ fragile trade truce at risk. The claim of such a bold espionage plot was also a potential source of embarrassment for a country hosting business and government leaders at a major event.
这些被中国否认的指控原本可能会破坏与特朗普的会谈，并危及两国脆弱的贸易休战。对于一个要在重要活动中接待商界和政府领导人的国家来说，如此直白的间谍阴谋指控可能也会引起尴尬。
3月，英伟达前首席执行官黄仁勋。《纽约时报》报道称，一名与黄仁勋关系密切的中国女商人被发现向北京传递情报。

China has carried on as if it were business as usual. And in a way, Beijing has already scored a win: The controversy has failed to derail the scheduled talks between Mr. Xi and Mr. Trump, who has downplayed the alleged spy plot.
中国在继续推进议程，仿佛什么都没有发生。在某种程度上，北京已经取得了一场胜利：这一争议未能破坏习近平与特朗普之间的预定会谈，特朗普已经淡化了被指存在的间谍阴谋。

Rather than declaring that he would confront China about the Nvidia scandal, Mr. Trump has said he does not intend to bring it up. “I don’t think you want to insult China just before you get there,” he told reporters outside the White House on Monday when asked about divisions within his administration about how tough to be on China.
特朗普并未宣布他将就英伟达丑闻与中国对抗，而是表示他不打算提及此事。周一，当在白宫外被问及其政府内部在对华强硬程度上的分歧时，他告诉记者：“我认为你不应该在去中国之前去得罪它。”

But the scandal is already costing China. On Monday, the Trump administration issued a rule to stop Chinese companies from accessing advanced Nvidia chips through data centers in third countries, and to require licenses for chip exports to companies in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil.
但这项丑闻已经让中国付出了代价。周一，特朗普政府发布了一项规定，阻止中国公司通过第三国的数据中心获取先进的英伟达芯片，并要求向马来西亚、新加坡、泰国、印度尼西亚和巴西的公司出口芯片必须获得许可。
China Needs to Ease Trade Concerns
中国需要缓解贸易担忧

China’s export machinery is practically unbeatable. This month, China reported that its exports exceeded its imports by more than $1 trillion in the first 10 months of this year, putting it on track to eclipse last year’s record.
中国的出口机器几乎不可战胜。中国本月报告称，今年前10个月贸易顺差超过1万亿美元，有望打破去年的纪录。

But as its factories have churned out solar panels, electric cars and other goods for consumers globally, China has faced pushback not only from the United States but from around the world. It needs to head off efforts by trading partners like the European Union to block its exports.
但随着中国工厂大量生产太阳能电池板、电动汽车和其他面向全球消费者的商品，中国不仅面临来自美国的抵制，还面临来自世界各地的抵制。它需要阻止欧盟等贸易伙伴阻碍其出口的努力。
That’s why China is billing the event as an opportunity for the region to champion free trade and oppose protectionism.
这就是为什么中国将此次活动宣传为该地区倡导自由贸易和反对保护主义的一个机会。
去年，中国合肥一家汽车工厂生产线上工作的员工。北京一直力推国产品牌、挤压外资品牌市场。

In reality, China has been turning inward. Beijing has sought to squeeze out foreign technology, electronics and auto brands in favor of Chinese firms. The Communist Party, which under Mr. Xi has tightened its grip on the economy, vowed last month to expand its presence inside internet companies. Shen Weizhong, a former policy planner with China’s Foreign Ministry, called the approach “manageable openness,” in which security weighs as heavily as growth.
实际上，中国一直在转向内向型发展。北京试图挤压外国技术、电子产品和汽车品牌的市场，扶持中国企业。在习近平领导下加强了对经济控制的共产党上个月誓言要扩大其在互联网公司内部的影响力。前中国外交部政策规划官员沈伟中称这种做法是“可控的开放”，其中安全与增长同等重要。
Mr. Xi’s willingness to turn the world’s dependence on Chinese goods into leverage has also alienated other countries.
习近平意在将世界对中国商品的依赖转化为筹码，这也疏远了其他国家。

Beijing imposed controls on exports of rare earths last year, and it has recently moved to restrict the exports of dozens of technologies, including drones, artificial intelligence models and agents, and know-how about advanced medicines and solar panels. China says these measures are a response to U.S. blacklists and export restrictions.
北京去年对稀土出口实施了管制，最近又采取行动限制数十项技术的出口，包括无人机、人工智能模型和智能体，以及有关先进药物和太阳能电池板的专业知识。中国表示，这些措施是对美国黑名单和出口限制的回应。

“Chinese leaders recognize that the golden era of globalization is over, and geoeconomic competition has become the new normal,” said Yuen Yuen Ang, a professor of political economy at Johns Hopkins University.
“中国领导人认识到，全球化的黄金时代已经结束，地缘经济竞争已成为新常态，”约翰斯·霍普金斯大学政治经济学教授洪源远表示。
Putin, Trump … and Kim?
普京、特朗普……还有金正恩？

Mr. Xi is expected to sit down with Mr. Trump and Mr. Putin on Thursday, a meeting that is without precedent. China’s Foreign Ministry on Monday called the meeting one “of groundbreaking significance.”
预计习近平将于周四与特朗普和普京举行会谈，这是一次史无前例的会议。中国外交部周一称这次会议“具有开创性意义”。

For Beijing, the gathering casts China as a power broker that can bring Washington and Moscow to the same table. Mr. Xi wants to show the world, and especially his own people, that China under his leadership is “consequential, influential and highly respected, with enormous convening power,” said Mr. Pei of Claremont McKenna.
对北京来说，这次聚会将中国塑造成一个能够让华盛顿和莫斯科坐到同一张谈判桌前的权力中间人。克莱蒙特·麦肯纳学院的裴敏欣表示，习近平希望向世界、特别是向本国人民展示，在他领导下的中国是“举足轻重、有影响力且备受尊重的，拥有巨大的号召力”。
But the optics are awkward.
但舆论观感有些尴尬。
5月，习近平与俄罗斯总统普京在北京。预计这两位领导人将在深圳与特朗普举行会谈，这将是一次史无前例的会议。

Mr. Trump said on Monday that he planned to discuss the war in Ukraine in Shenzhen. Beijing is reluctant to take the lead on peace talks, said Zhao Long, a senior research fellow at the Shanghai Institutes for International Studies, lest it create “the wrong impression” that “major powers are dividing up the interests of other countries.”
特朗普周一表示，他计划在深圳讨论乌克兰战争。上海国际问题研究院高级研究员赵隆表示，北京不愿在和平谈判中牵头，以免造成“大国正在瓜分其他国家利益”的“错误印象”。

And Mr. Trump has raised the possibility of another guest: the North Korean dictator, Kim Jong-un. He told reporters on Monday as he left the White House: “And we may meet with Kim Jong Un, also. So, that’ll be good. We could — we have a chance to accomplish a lot.”
特朗普还提出了另一位客人的可能性：朝鲜独裁者金正恩。他周一离开白宫时告诉记者：“我们可能还会见金正恩。所以，那会很好。我们可以——我们有机会取得很多成就。”

A spokesman for China’s foreign ministry, Guo Jiakun, asked on Tuesday if Mr. Kim would be attending, said: “I do not have information on this.” Russian state news agencies reported that Mr. Putin could meet with Mr. Kim if the North Korean leader travels to China, citing Dmitri S. Peskov, the Kremlin’s spokesman.
中国外交部发言人郭嘉昆周二在被问及金正恩是否会出席时表示：“我们没有这方面的信息。”俄罗斯国家通讯社援引克里姆林宫发言人德米特里·S·佩斯科夫的话报道称，如果这位朝鲜领导人前往中国，普京可能会与他会面。
Berry Wang、Keith Bradsher、Ruoxin Zhang和Siyi Zhao对本文有报道和研究贡献。
David Pierson报道中国外交政策和中国与世界的经济与文化交互。他从事新闻工作已超过20年。

items.body:
KURT CAMPBELL2026年11月18日

Illustration by Sam Whitney/The New York Times

A vexing feature of President Trump’s foreign policy is his unfailing attraction to the world’s two dominant strongmen, President Xi Jinping of China and President Vladimir Putin of Russia. Like a deer drawn toward the intriguing smell of the hunters’ blind, Mr. Trump seems compelled to engage with both authoritarian leaders.

特朗普总统外交政策中一个令人费解的特点是，他总是被世界上两位处于主导地位的强人所吸引，也就是中国国家主席习近平和俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京。就像鹿被猎人掩体散发出的迷人气息所吸引一样，特朗普似乎情不自禁地要与这两位威权领导人来往。

Mr. Trump’s desire has produced generally anticlimactic bilateral engagements so far in his second term. The 2025 Alaska summit with Mr. Putin made no headway on ending the war in Ukraine. The three recent meetings with Mr. Xi made little progress in easing trade tensions or increasing artificial intelligence safeguards. Now, all three leaders are set to convene in an unusual trilateral forum on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation in Shenzhen, China, this week.

迄今为止，在特朗普的第二任期内，他的这种意愿所带来的双边接触总体上令人扫兴。2025年，他与普京在阿拉斯加举行的峰会在结束乌克兰战争方面没有取得任何进展。近期与习近平的三次会晤在缓解贸易紧张局势或增加人工智能安全保障方面进展甚微。如今，本周在中国深圳举行的亚太经合组织会议间隙，这三位领导人将在一场不同寻常的三边论坛上齐聚一堂。

For Americans and their like-minded partners, little that is beneficial can come from the meeting.

对于美国人及其志同道合的伙伴来说，这次会议几乎不会带来任何有益的结果。

Most American multilateral gatherings in recent decades have convened states that largely shared our national interests, like the maritime democracies of the so-called QUAD — India, Japan, Australia and the United States. This would be the first time that a sitting American president has jointly met with the leaders of China and Russia, who represent systems and approaches to global affairs that are widely considered antithetical to American interests.

近几十年来，美国的大多数多边集会召集的都是在很大程度上与我们享有共同国家利益的国家，比如四方安全对话(QUAD)中的海洋民主国家——印度、日本、澳大利亚和美国。这将是现任美国总统首次与中俄领导人共同会晤，这两位领导人代表的体制和处理全球事务的方式被广泛认为与美国利益背道而驰。

Mr. Trump’s spokesmen and sycophants say doing so will advance peace in Europe and buy time while the United States builds resilience in its critical minerals stockpiles. It is difficult for them to explain the president’s obvious zeal for the gathering when he is so evidently unenthusiastic about Group of 7 summits with the seven richest democracies, or meetings with European Union leaders. It is even harder given what Mr. Xi and Mr. Putin are doing behind the scenes to undermine America.

特朗普的发言人和阿谀奉承者表示，这样做将促进欧洲的和平，并为美国在关键矿产储备上形成韧性争取时间。他们很难解释总统为什么对此次集会表现出巨大的热情，对由七个最富有的民主国家组成的七国集团峰会或与欧盟领导人的会晤却明显缺乏兴趣。而考虑到习近平和普京在幕后为削弱美国所做的一切，这一切就更加难以理解了。

China is the principal backer of Russia’s war against Ukraine, providing essential supplies that keep Moscow’s missiles and drones flying. Russia is giving Iran satellite imaging and overhead targeting data even as Iran strikes U.S. military assets in the Gulf region. Chinese companies have provided Iran with crucial missile components. Joint Chinese and Russian military exercises in the western Pacific are increasingly active around Japan and near contested island territories. Beneath the appearance of accord at the trilateral summit, Mr. Trump will be making nice with opponents who have daggers drawn against our allies and partners in three of the world’s most dangerous spots.

中国是俄罗斯对乌战争的主要支持者，为莫斯科的导弹和无人机提供维持运转的关键物资。即使在伊朗打击美国在海湾地区的军事资产之际，俄罗斯仍在向伊朗提供卫星成像和高空目标数据。中国企业向伊朗提供了关键的导弹部件。中俄在西太平洋的联合军事演习在日本周边和有争议的岛屿领土附近日益活跃。在三边峰会表面上的和谐之下，特朗普实际上是在向对手示好，它们正在世界上最危险的三个地区对我们的盟友和伙伴拔刀相向。

The Trump administration completely misunderstands the complexities of the Russia-China relationship. In that, it is not alone: There are few bilateral relationships that American strategists have historically so thoroughly misdiagnosed. In the 1960s, the best and the brightest in the United States were very late in realizing the opportunity presented by the Sino-Soviet split; now they underestimate just how significant the Russia-China partnership has become.

特朗普政府完全误解了俄中关系的复杂性。在这方面，它并不孤单：在历史上，很少有哪对双边关系被美国战略家误诊得如此彻底。在20世纪60年代，美国最优秀、最聪明的人迟迟没能意识到中苏交恶带来的机遇；如今，他们又低估了俄中伙伴关系已经变得多么重要。

Since Mr. Xi came to power in 2012, he and Mr. Putin have met officially about 50 times, an extraordinary tempo of high-level diplomacy. In theory, Russia and China, with their history of distrust, border disputes and conflicting ambitions, should not get along. In practice, these two like-minded men have built one of the most durable security partnerships on the planet. Each side no doubt worries about the future of that collaboration, but for now it is deeply consequential and immune to efforts to split them apart.

习近平自2012年上台以来已经与普京举行了约50次正式会晤，这是一种不同寻常的高层外交节奏。理论上，两国的历史充斥着不信任、边界争端和相互冲突的野心，本不应如此和睦相处。但在实践中，这两位志同道合的人建立起了地球上最持久的安全伙伴关系之一。毫无疑问，双方都对这种合作的未来感到担忧，但就目前而言，这种合作影响深远，并且不受试图将他们分开的努力的影响。

What will the three leaders discuss at this summit? China is rapidly and quietly building up its nuclear arsenal, which is much smaller than Russia’s or America’s, and so it will seek to avoid any negotiations that would keep it from catching up. Russia will talk only in ideological generalities about peace in Europe. The United States will be loath to beg for assistance in ending the war in Iran, particularly from the two countries most actively supporting Tehran. Russia will not want to talk much about A.I., as doing so will highlight how it is badly behind. Boosting global energy supplies is an issue tangled up in the disruptions in the Persian Gulf. Global development needs would be an awkward topic now that the U.S. has sharply reduced its humanitarian assistance efforts.

这三位领导人将在这次峰会上讨论什么？中国正在迅速而悄悄地扩充其核武库，其规模远小于俄罗斯或美国，因此它将寻求避免任何会阻止其迎头赶上的谈判。俄罗斯将只会在意识形态的泛泛之谈中讨论欧洲和平问题。美国将不愿乞求协助结束伊朗战争，尤其考虑到这是两个最积极支持德黑兰的国家。俄罗斯不会想多谈人工智能，因为这样做会凸显其严重落后的情况。增加全球能源供应是一个与波斯湾局势动荡纠缠不清的问题。鉴于美国已大幅削减其人道主义援助努力，全球发展需求现在将成为一个尴尬的话题。

The lack of a clear agenda for the trilateral summit is going to make Mr. Xi uncomfortable, and he is unlikely to agree to any spontaneous deals. He is focused on achieving a fourth five-year term in office next year, the longest stretch in power of any recent Chinese leader, and he does not like surprises. Given Mr. Trump’s proclivity for improvisation, Mr. Xi will be wary of any attempt at a diplomatic breakthrough.

So the primary consequence of the trilateral summit in Shenzhen may be the message conveyed by three would-be strongmen standing together astride the planet, surveying the scene. This will send shivers among America’s traditional allies — clearly a plus for Mr. Putin and Mr. Xi, and probably irrelevant to Mr. Trump. Even if the discussions focus only on the stonework in Mr. Trump’s new ballroom, the flight time from Moscow to Shenzhen or the quality of the local Cantonese cuisine, projecting the image of these three leaders meeting together may well be the real purpose at work in Moscow and Beijing.

因此，深圳三边峰会的主要结果可能是三位热衷于铁腕统治的领导人并肩屹立、审视全局，这将让美国的传统盟友感到不寒而栗——这对普京和习近平来说显然是个加分项，而对特朗普来说可能无关紧要。即使讨论只集中在特朗普新宴会厅的石材工艺、从莫斯科到深圳的飞行时间，或是当地粤菜的质量上，展示这三位领导人齐聚一堂的形象很可能才是莫斯科和北京方面真正在努力达成的目的。

Kurt Campbell是咨询公司亚洲集团的董事长和创始人。

A vexing feature of President Trump’s foreign policy is his unfailing attraction to the world’s two dominant strongmen, President Xi Jinping of China and President Vladimir Putin of Russia. Like a deer drawn toward the intriguing smell of the hunters’ blind, Mr. Trump seems compelled to engage with both authoritarian leaders.
特朗普总统外交政策中一个令人费解的特点是，他总是被世界上两位处于主导地位的强人所吸引，也就是中国国家主席习近平和俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京。就像鹿被猎人掩体散发出的迷人气息所吸引一样，特朗普似乎情不自禁地要与这两位威权领导人来往。

Mr. Trump’s desire has produced generally anticlimactic bilateral engagements so far in his second term. The 2025 Alaska summit with Mr. Putin made no headway on ending the war in Ukraine. The three recent meetings with Mr. Xi made little progress in easing trade tensions or increasing artificial intelligence safeguards. Now, all three leaders are set to convene in an unusual trilateral forum on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation in Shenzhen, China, this week.
迄今为止，在特朗普的第二任期内，他的这种意愿所带来的双边接触总体上令人扫兴。2025年，他与普京在阿拉斯加举行的峰会在结束乌克兰战争方面没有取得任何进展。近期与习近平的三次会晤在缓解贸易紧张局势或增加人工智能安全保障方面进展甚微。如今，本周在中国深圳举行的亚太经合组织会议间隙，这三位领导人将在一场不同寻常的三边论坛上齐聚一堂。
For Americans and their like-minded partners, little that is beneficial can come from the meeting.
对于美国人及其志同道合的伙伴来说，这次会议几乎不会带来任何有益的结果。

Most American multilateral gatherings in recent decades have convened states that largely shared our national interests, like the maritime democracies of the so-called QUAD — India, Japan, Australia and the United States. 近几十年来，美国的大多数多边集会召集的都是在很大程度上与我们享有共同国家利益的国家，比如四方安全对话(QUAD)中的海洋民主国家——印度、日本、澳大利亚和美国。这将是现任美国总统首次与中俄领导人共同会晤，这两位领导人代表的体制和处理全球事务的方式被广泛认为与美国利益背道而驰。

China is the principal backer of Russia’s war against Ukraine, providing essential supplies that keep Moscow’s missiles and drones flying. Russia is giving Iran satellite imaging and overhead targeting data even as Iran strikes U.S. military assets in the Gulf region. Chinese companies have provided Iran with crucial missile components. Beneath the appearance of accord at the trilateral summit, Mr. Trump will be making nice with opponents who have daggers drawn against our allies and partners in three of the world’s most dangerous spots.
中国是俄罗斯对乌战争的主要支持者，为莫斯科的导弹和无人机提供维持运转的关键物资。即使在伊朗打击美国在海湾地区的军事资产之际，俄罗斯仍在向伊朗提供卫星成像和高空目标数据。中国企业向伊朗提供了关键的导弹部件。中俄在西太平洋的联合军事演习在日本周边和有争议的岛屿领土附近日益活跃。在三边峰会表面上的和谐之下，特朗普实际上是在向对手示好，它们正在世界上最危险的三个地区对我们的盟友和伙伴拔刀相向。

The Trump administration completely misunderstands the complexities of the Russia-China relationship. In that, it is not alone: There are few bilateral relationships that American strategists have historically so thoroughly misdiagnosed. In the 1960s, the best and the brightest in the United States were very late in realizing the opportunity presented by the Sino-Soviet split; now they underestimate just how significant the Russia-China partnership has become.

Since Mr. Xi came to power in 2012, he and Mr. Putin have met officially about 50 times, an extraordinary tempo of high-level diplomacy. In practice, these two like-minded men have built one of the most durable security partnerships on the planet. Each side no doubt worries about the future of that collaboration, but for now it is deeply consequential and immune to efforts to split them apart.
习近平自2012年上台以来已经与普京举行了约50次正式会晤，这是一种不同寻常的高层外交节奏。理论上，两国的历史充斥着不信任、边界争端和相互冲突的野心，本不应如此和睦相处。但在实践中，这两位志同道合的人建立起了地球上最持久的安全伙伴关系之一。毫无疑问，双方都对这种合作的未来感到担忧，但就目前而言，这种合作影响深远，并且不受试图将他们分开的努力的影响。

What will the three leaders discuss at this summit? China is rapidly and quietly building up its nuclear arsenal, which is much smaller than Russia’s or America’s, and so it will seek to avoid any negotiations that would keep it from catching up. Russia will talk only in ideological generalities about peace in Europe. The United States will be loath to beg for assistance in ending the war in Iran, particularly from the two countries most actively supporting Tehran. Russia will not want to talk much about A.I., as doing so will highlight how it is badly behind. Boosting global energy supplies is an issue tangled up in the disruptions in the Persian Gulf. items.body:
黄安伟, DUSTIN VOLZ2026年11月18日

对间谍活动的怀疑加剧了华盛顿与北京在人工智能问题上的相互猜疑。 Haiyun Jiang/The New York Times

When President Trump and Xi Jinping, the leader of China, met earlier this fall, they sounded committed to finding common ground on calibrating the rapid development of advanced artificial intelligence.

今年秋季早些时候，特朗普总统与中国领导人习近平会晤时，双方似乎都致力于在如何规范先进人工智能的快速发展方面寻求共识。

“We have both the capability and responsibility to develop and manage A.I. for good and ensure that the development of A.I. is always under human control and serves the well-being of the people,” Mr. Xi said in September in the grand foyer of the White House.

“中美两国都是人工智能大国，有能力也有责任发展好、管控好人工智能，确保人工智能发展始终受控于人、造福于民，”习近平9月在白宫宏伟的门厅里说。

Mr. Trump leaned into that spirit, saying, “The decisions we make in these areas today can promote peace and prosperity for decades and decades to come.” But he has called fears of A.I. threats a “hoax,” and earlier that week said at the United Nations that he would label artificial intelligence “super intelligence” to give it a better branding.

特朗普呼应了这种精神，他说：“我们今天在这些领域做出的决定，可以促进未来几十年的和平与繁荣。”但他曾称对人工智能威胁的担忧是“骗局”，并在那周早些时候在联合国表示，他将把人工智能称为“超级智能”，给它一个更好的品牌形象。

On the eve of their third leadership summit of the year, the two men and their administrations have made little if any progress on negotiating A.I. safety issues and development guidelines, despite growing fears about the technology, current and former U.S. officials say.

现任和前任美国官员表示，在今年第三次领导人峰会前夕，尽管人们对这项技术的担忧与日俱增，但两人及其政府在谈判人工智能安全问题和发展指导方针方面，几乎没有取得任何进展。

And that was before Jensen Huang was forced to resign last week as chief executive of Nvidia, the U.S. technology giant that supplies computer chips fueling the A.I. boom.

而这还是在黄仁勋上周被迫辞去英伟达首席执行官一职之前发生的事情，英伟达供应的计算机芯片正是推动人工智能热潮的动力。

Mr. Huang stepped down after The New York Times reported last month that the U.S. had gathered intelligence showing that a Chinese businesswoman in Singapore with whom he had a close relationship might have been secretly working or in contact with China’s main spy agency. Mr. Huang has publicly admitted that he had an affair.

《纽约时报》上月报道称，美国收集的情报显示，一名与黄仁勋关系密切的新加坡中国女商人可能一直在秘密为中国主要间谍机构工作或与其有联系，随后黄仁勋辞职。黄仁勋已公开承认他有婚外情。

今年5月，黄仁勋在北京人民大会堂出席中国国务院总理李强与美国商界代表的会晤，并向媒体发表讲话。

Advancements in technology — and particularly on A.I. — have become a focal point in the superpowers’ economic and military rivalry in recent years, but never have those issues been more in the spotlight.

近年来，技术的进步——尤其是人工智能的进步——已成为这两个超级大国经济和军事竞争的焦点，但这些问题从未像现在这样备受瞩目。

“The primary point of competition between us is certainly on A.I., quantum computing, biotech, cyber, all those issues,” said R. Nicholas Burns, a former career U.S. diplomat who was ambassador to China in the Biden administration.

“我们之间的主要竞争点肯定在人工智能、量子计算、生物技术、网络等所有这些问题上，”曾在美国拜登政府担任驻华大使的前职业外交官R·尼古拉斯·伯恩斯说。

“But obviously we’ve got a self-interest, and I think they do too,” he added, “in making sure the competition doesn’t veer off in a direction that would be destabilizing and potentially increase the probability of a conflict.”

“但显然，我们有自身的利益考量，我认为他们也是如此，”他还说。“我们要确保竞争不会偏离正轨，以免造成不稳定，并可能增加冲突爆发的概率。”

Secretary of State Marco Rubio said last week that the governments have had conversations about A.I. safety “sort of at the technical level.” “Obviously, we’ve heard their perspective, they’ve heard ours, but that’s still a work in progress,” he said.

国务卿鲁比奥上周表示，两国政府已经在“某种程度上在技术层面”就人工智能安全进行了对话。“显然，我们听取了他们的观点，他们也听取了我们的观点，但这仍是一项正在进行中的工作，”他说。

One reason there has been little momentum is that the two nations have differing views of the greatest risks posed by A.I., the current and former U.S. officials say.

现任和前任美国官员表示，进展乏力的原因之一是，两国对人工智能带来的最大风险有着不同的看法。

In the United States, officials, executives and researchers talk about the possibility of A.I. becoming autonomous and working on its own outside human control or even dominating humans.

在美国，官员、高管和研究人员谈论的是人工智能可能实现自主化、在不受人类控制的情况下自行工作，甚至统治人类的可能性。

That is a concern in China, too, but its government appears to be more worried about how A.I. could be used by humans to undermine the Chinese Communist Party.

这在中国也是一个令人担忧的问题，但中国政府似乎更担心人工智能会被人利用来动摇中国共产党。

At the same time, the party’s main spy and counterintelligence agency, the Ministry of State Security, aims to use A.I. for intelligence gathering both in the country and overseas, The Times has reported.

据《纽约时报》报道，与此同时，中共的主要间谍和反情报机构国家安全部，旨在利用人工智能在国内和海外收集情报。

Suspicions about espionage heighten the mutual distrust in Washington and Beijing over A.I. issues. Each side thinks the other is engaged in spying to learn more about rival A.I. secrets and to dominate development faster, the officials said.

关于间谍活动的怀疑加剧了华盛顿和北京在人工智能问题上的互不信任。官员们说，双方都认为对方在从事间谍活动，以了解更多关于竞争对手人工智能机密的信息，并更快地主导技术发展。

The murky trade and spying scandal involving Mr. Huang and Nvidia looms over the meeting between Mr. Trump and Mr. Xi scheduled for Thursday in Shenzhen, a technology and manufacturing hub in southern China.

涉及黄仁勋和英伟达扑朔迷离的交易与间谍丑闻给特朗普和习近平的会晤蒙上了阴影，峰会定于周四在中国南方科技和制造业中心深圳举行。

In his second term, Mr. Trump has ordered the U.S. government to loosen export restrictions to China on advanced chips. But on Monday, the Trump administration announced that it was moving forward with a new rule that would limit China’s ability to access certain chips through the use of data centers in other countries.

在第二任期内，特朗普已下令美国政府放宽对中国先进芯片的出口限制。但在周一，特朗普政府宣布正在推进一项新规定，该规定将限制中国通过利用其他国家的数据中心获取某些芯片的能力。

去年在华盛顿会议中心举办的一场由英伟达参与的展览活动中，与会者参观展出的计算技术。

The policy on advanced chips is separate from the safety issues about A.I. development. The nascent dialogue on safety is being run by the Treasury Department. Critics say the talks are virtually nonexistent, though Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent insists they will happen.

关于先进芯片的政策与人工智能发展的安全问题是分开推进的。目前由财政部主导着关于安全问题的初步对话。批评人士表示，这些谈判实际上并不存在，尽管财政部长斯科特·贝森特坚称它们将会进行。

The governments “expect to exchange best practices for evaluating and testing advanced models before their release, and for keeping human judgment firmly in command of this technology,” he said last week.

他上周表示，两国政府“期望就发布前评估和测试先进模型的最佳实践，以及让这项技术牢牢受控于人类判断的最佳实践进行交流”。

He added that they are “establishing a direct channel to ensure that either nation can promptly alert the other to serious incidents involving” A.I. models.

他还说，双方正在“建立一个直接渠道，以确保任何一国都能及时向另一国通报”涉及人工智能模型的“严重事件”。

As he eventually did with Mr. Trump, Mr. Xi agreed to start a dialogue on A.I. with the Biden administration. The first meeting was held in Geneva in May 2024. Mr. Biden’s aides had hoped China would send officials from the three agencies most involved in monitoring or regulating A.I. development, including the Ministry of State Security, the spy agency.

正如他与特朗普最终所做的那样，习近平同意与拜登政府就人工智能展开对话。首次会议于2024年5月在日内瓦举行。拜登的助手曾希望中国派出最密切参与监控或监管人工智能发展的三个机构的官员，其中包括间谍机构国家安全部。

But China sent foreign ministry officials disappointing the Americans, former U.S. officials said. The two sides made little headway.

items.body:
东日本旅客铁道公司11月18日宣布，交通IC卡Suica的新形象角色确定为一只紫色兔子，将于2027年3月接替沿用多年的企鹅形象。公司此前邀请年轻创作者设计新角色，从中选出三个候选方案，并于9月举行网络投票。新角色的名称将另行公开征集。
获选的紫色兔子象征向未来跃进，颜色由代表安心的蓝色与代表感动的红色融合而成，同时寓意倾听周围的声音。其余两个候选方案分别是象征连接人们生活的松鼠，以及没有特定动物原型的橙色角色。
该公司计划于2027年3月举行企鹅形象的告别及角色交接活动，并希望以新角色象征Suica的功能改革。11月18日也是Suica于2001年正式推出服务的纪念日。
（日本经济新闻）

quote.text: 东日本旅客铁路公司宣布，将于2026年秋为其发行的Suica交通卡增设二维码支付及汇款功能，并提高支付额度，使其从交通票证扩展为可在车站商业设施进行高额消费的支付工具，以应对PayPay等无现金服务的竞争。 该公司同时表示，旗下交通卡使用逾25年的吉祥物形象Suica企鹅将在2026年度末“毕业”，新吉祥物尚未确定。 Suica交通卡自2001年推出以来，发卡量已突破 1 亿张。由坂崎千春创作的企鹅形象长期作为吉祥物，衍生出大量周边商品与专门店。 （日本经济新闻 1，2）

items.body:
IAN AUSTEN2026年11月18日

加拿大总理马克·卡尼与中国领导人习近平周二在深圳会晤。 Adrian Wyld/The Canadian Press, via Associated Press

Prime Minister Mark Carney of Canada and China’s leader, Xi Jinping, have struck an agreement to reduce some tariffs between their countries, a largely symbolic move that shows relations between the two countries are warming as Canada’s ties to the United States falter.

加拿大总理卡尼和中国领导人习近平达成了一项降低两国间部分关税的协议，这在很大程度上是一个象征性的举措，表明随着加拿大与美国的联系出现动摇，中加两国关系正在回暖。

While the expanded trade between China and Canada resulting from the accord in the Chinese tech and financial hub Shenzhen will be modest, involving just $280 million in exports, the pact — as well as the seemingly amicable meeting — illustrates a contrast to Mr. Carney’s relationship with President Trump. Earlier this year, Mr. Carney said that the United States was “at war” with Canada after trade negotiations between the two countries collapsed in acrimony.

这项在中国的科技和金融中心深圳达成的协议将使中加贸易规模有所扩大，但增幅有限，仅涉及2.8亿美元的出口。不过，这项协议以及此次显得颇为友好的会晤与卡尼和特朗普总统的关系形成了鲜明对比。今年早些时候，美加贸易谈判在激烈争吵中破裂后，卡尼曾表示美国正在与加拿大“交战”。

Talks are restarting between Canada and the United States but there is no indication that Washington will back away from key irritants including tariffs of up to 50 percent on Canadian autos, steel and aluminum.

加拿大和美国正在重启谈判，但没有迹象表明华盛顿会在主要摩擦因素上让步，包括对加拿大汽车、钢铁和铝征收高达50%的关税。

Since entering politics last year, Mr. Carney has been traveling the world to diversify Canada’s economic and political ties away from the United States. Those efforts include current talks to make Canada the European Union’s first associate member and Mr. Carney’s second formal meeting this year with Mr. Xi.

自去年进入政界以来，卡尼一直在世界各地周游，致力于使加拿大的经济和政治关系多元化，减少对美国的依赖。这些努力包括目前旨在使加拿大成为欧盟首个准成员国的谈判，以及卡尼今年与习近平的第二次正式会晤。

“The stabilization of our bilateral trade arrangement is indicative of how we can work together more broadly, pragmatically, to solve problems,” Mr. Carney said at the start of the meeting with Mr. Xi on Tuesday.

“双边贸易安排的稳定表明，我们可以在更广泛、更务实的层面上合作解决问题，”卡尼在周二与习近平会晤开始时说。

He added that Canada is ahead of schedule with its goal of a 50 percent increase in exports to China by the end of the decade.

他还说，加拿大在实现本十年末对华出口增长50%的目标方面进度超前。

China and Canada were in a trade war after the Canadian government under Justin Trudeau, Canada’s former prime minister, followed the lead of the Biden administration and imposed a 100 percent tariff on Chinese-made electric vehicles. China responded with tariffs on a variety of Canadian products, particularly canola, an oil seed.

加拿大前总理特鲁多领导的加拿大政府效仿拜登政府，对中国制造的电动汽车征收100%的关税，此后中加两国曾陷入贸易战。作为回应，中国对多种加拿大产品征收关税，特别是油料作物油菜籽。

That dispute was largely resolved in January during the first formal meeting between Mr. Xi and Mr. Carney. China lifted its canola tariff after Canada agreed to allow a relatively small number of Chinese E.V.s into the country at a minimal tariff rate.

这一争端在今年1月习近平和卡尼的首次正式会晤中基本得到解决。在加拿大同意以极低的关税税率允许相对少量的中国电动汽车进入该国后，中国取消了对油菜籽的关税。

Before Tuesday’s meeting, Mr. Xi attempted to put the frosty relations firmly in the past, which were worsened by China’s arrest in 2018 of two Canadians in retaliation for Canada’s detaining a Chinese telecommunications executive under an extradition request from the United States.

在周二的会晤之前，习近平试图将冰冷的关系彻底留在过去——2018年，中国逮捕了两名加拿大人，以报复加拿大根据美国的引渡请求拘留一名中国电信高管，这使得两国关系进一步恶化。

“The development of Chinese-Canadian relations over the years has provided us with an important lesson,” Mr. Xi said at the start of the meeting. “We must respect each other, pursue equality and mutual benefit and seek common ground while setting aside differences.”

“中加关系这些年发展历程给我们的重要启示，就是相互尊重、平等互利、求同存异。中方愿同加方一道努力，”习近平在会晤开始时说。

Tuesday’s announcement will largely eliminate tariffs on frozen Canadian pork and several seafoods. Both were caught up in China’s E.V. retaliation. Canada, in turn, will continue to suspend tariffs on some Chinese steel and aluminum products that were set to expire at the end of the year. It will also expand the list of products covered by the suspension.

周二的公告将在基本取消对加拿大冷冻猪肉和若干海产品的关税。这两种产品都被卷入了中国对电动汽车的报复行动中。相应地，加拿大将继续暂停对部分中国钢铁和铝产品的关税，这些关税原定于年底到期。加拿大还将扩大暂免关税的产品清单。

A Canadian government document said that since March car plants in China had exported 16,211 vehicles to Canada under an annual quota of 49,000. Half of those autos, it said, are priced at under 35,000 Canadian dollars (about $24,500). It said that a second Chinese automaker had been given safety approval by Canada for its cars. That company, which the government will not name, plans to offer only cars that cost less than 35,000 dollars, Canada’s price limit target.

一份加拿大政府文件称，自3月以来，中国汽车工厂在4.9万辆的年度配额下向加拿大出口了16211辆汽车。文件称，其中一半汽车的售价低于3.5万加元（约合2.45万美元）。文件还指出，第二家中国汽车制造商的汽车已获得加拿大安全认证。该公司（政府未透露其名称）计划仅销售价格低于3.5万加元的汽车，这正是加拿大的价格上限目标。

On Monday in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, Mr. Carney said that Canada would turn to China, Japan and Europe to save its auto industry if it was unable to eliminate Mr. Trump’s tariffs.

周一在柬埔寨金边，卡尼表示，如果无法取消特朗普的关税，加拿大将转向中国、日本和欧洲来拯救其汽车工业。

The meeting between Mr. Carney and Mr. Xi came ahead of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum, which is being held in Shenzhen later this week.

卡尼和习近平的会晤是在亚太经济合作组织论坛之前举行的，该论坛将于本周晚些时候在深圳举行。

Since his address to the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, in January, Mr. Carney has become something of a champion for nations with advanced economies that are not super powers — a group he calls “middle powers.”

自今年1月在瑞士达沃斯世界经济论坛发表演讲以来，卡尼已成为那些非超级大国的发达经济体国家的代言人，他将这一群体称为“中等强国”。

But the main event of the APEC summit will be a meeting between Mr. Xi, Mr. Trump and Vladimir V. Putin of Russia.

但亚太经合组织峰会的主要议程将是习近平、特朗普和俄罗斯总统普京之间的会晤。

When asked earlier in his Asia trip about the superpower summit, Mr. Carney repeated Canada’s support for Ukraine following Russia’s invasion.

在此次亚洲之行的早些时候，当被问及这场超级大国峰会时，卡尼重申了加拿大在俄罗斯入侵后对乌克兰的支持。

Canadian officials said they do not expect that Mr. Trump and Mr. Carney will meet in Shenzhen. Mr. Carney is also unlikely to meet Mr. Putin. He said over the weekend that he would not boycott a summit group photo including Mr. Putin, but only out of respect for China.

加拿大官员表示，他们预计特朗普和卡尼不会在深圳会面。卡尼也不太可能与普京会面。他周末表示，他不会抵制包括普京在内的峰会合影，但这仅仅是出于对中国的尊重。

艾莎, MURPHY ZHAO2026年11月18日

9月，特朗普总统和第一夫人梅拉尼娅在白宫欢迎中国国家主席习近平和夫人彭丽媛。 Haiyun Jiang/The New York Times

In front of the cameras, President Trump and China’s Xi Jinping have showcased a budding friendship, cemented by state visits, friendly pats on the arm and the occasional shared laugh.

在镜头前，特朗普总统与中国国家主席习近平展现出一种日渐升温的友谊，国事访问、友好的轻拍手臂以及偶尔的开怀大笑巩固了这段友谊。

But the public cordiality masks a different reality. Their governments are hardening their economic defenses and putting up new barriers to trade and investment. It has become more difficult for the two countries to invest, trade or do business with each other.

但公开的友好掩盖了另一种现实。两国政府正在强化各自的经济防御并设置新的贸易和投资壁垒。两国之间的投资、贸易或商业往来变得更加困难。

More good will is expected when Mr. Trump arrives in the Chinese city of Shenzhen this week for his third meeting with Mr. Xi this year. On Tuesday, China called the rule a “textbook case of economic coercion and long-arm jurisdiction” that “disrupts the stability of global industrial and supply chains.”

Beijing has designated more technologies as strategically vital, placing tighter controls on their export. Washington has proposed barring American investment in Chinese biotechnology, hypersonic weapons and artificial intelligence.

这是中美两国近几周以国家安全为由将各自经济的新领域列为禁区的一系列举措中的最新一项。北京已将更多技术指定为具有战略重要性，并对其出口实施了更严格的控制。华盛顿则提议禁止美国投资中国的生物技术、高超音速武器和人工智能领域。

The confrontation has spilled beyond their two countries’ borders into global supply chains. China is building a fortress around technologies and critical materials on which much of the world depends, forcing other countries and multinational companies to contend with the fallout.

这种对抗已经蔓延至两国边界之外的全球供应链。中国正在围绕世界上许多国家所依赖的技术和关键材料建立堡垒，迫使其他国家和跨国公司应对由此产生的影响。

“There are more barriers than bridges being built,” said Ben Kostrzewa, a partner at the law firm Hogan Lovells in Hong Kong. “Each of these moves on its own is another brick in the wall and it is becoming harder and harder to invest in the other country.”

霍金路伟律师事务所(Hogan Lovells)驻香港合伙人本·科斯特泽瓦表示：“建起的壁垒多于桥梁。这些举措中的每一项本身都是墙上的一块砖，在对方国家投资正变得越来越困难。”

The steady buildup of those barriers began nearly a decade ago as a tit-for-tat tariff war during Mr. Trump’s first term. It has evolved into a far broader showdown for economic and technological supremacy.

这些壁垒的稳步建立始于近十年前特朗普首个任期内的一场针锋相对的关税战。如今，它已演变成一场在经济和技术主导权方面更为广泛的较量。

China, in particular, has shifted its tactics. Once largely content to answer American tariffs and sanctions with reciprocal measures that were often symbolic, Beijing is now going on the offensive. It is wielding its dominance in manufacturing and critical supply chains to remind Washington — and the rest of the world — of the costs of confronting it.

中国方面已经改变了策略。北京曾经在很大程度上满足于用往往只是象征意义上的对等措施来回应美国的关税和制裁，但现在正采取攻势。中国正利用其在制造业和关键供应链中的主导地位，提醒华盛顿以及世界其他地区与其对抗的代价。

竞争在去年降至冰点，当时双方征收的关税过高，等同于事实上的贸易禁运。随后，中国威胁要收紧对稀土的控制，稀土是智能手机、电动汽车以及战斗机等各种产品中必不可少的材料。

2025年10月，特朗普和习近平通过同意休战和相互进行国事访问缓解了紧张局势。

When Mr. Xi landed in Maryland in September, he was welcomed on the tarmac by Mr. Trump. There have been raised glasses, shared walks and moments of banter.

After Mr. Xi’s visit two months ago, the two governments agreed to extend their yearlong truce and reduce tariffs on $60 billion worth of goods. Yet neither side formally confirmed the extension until hours before the agreement was set to expire, just a week before Mr. Trump’s planned arrival in China.

在习近平两个月前访问之后，两国政府同意将为期一年的休战期延长，并降低价值600亿美元商品的关税。然而，直到协议到期前几个小时，也就是特朗普计划抵达中国前一周，双方才正式确认延期。

Even then, the reprieve was limited. The renewed truce, which suspended certain tariffs and export controls, runs only through January.

即使如此，这种喘息之机也是有限的。新的休战协议暂停了部分关税和出口管制，但仅持续到明年1月。

9月，习近平访美，机场铺设了红地毯迎接他。

And despite Beijing’s pledge to ease restrictions on exports of rare-earth metals and other critical minerals, some American companies still struggle to obtain supplies, said Erin Browne, the U.S. Treasury Department’s under secretary for international affairs.

美国财政部负责国际事务的副部长埃琳·布朗表示，尽管北京承诺放宽对稀土金属和其他关键矿产的出口限制，但一些美国公司在获取供应方面仍面临困难。

“We’re making sure that we’re getting equal treatment across companies, across sectors, but also across materials or rare earths,” Ms. Browne said. “The strength of the relationship between our two presidents goes a long way in helping to move that along.”

Yet the personal rapport has done little to restrain an emboldened China, which has signaled it is no longer afraid of escalating economic warfare.

然而，这种个人交情几乎无法约束更加自信的中国，中国已发出信号，不再畏惧经济战的升级。

随着美国将中国企业列入黑名单，中国也加强了反制。它建立了新的法律机制来阻断外国制裁，而且中国企业已经在中国法院对遵守美国限制措施的外国企业（包括摩根大通和花旗银行）提起诉讼。

This year, Beijing introduced sweeping rules empowering regulators to inspect corporate records and prevent executives from leaving China if their companies are found to be helping to shift supply chains out of the country.

今年，北京出台了广泛的规定，授权监管机构检查企业记录，并且如果发现企业协助将供应链转移出中国，可阻止高管离境。

It has also established a national security review system for foreign investments, using it to block Meta’s $2 billion acquisition of Manus and SoftBank’s $5.4 billion takeover of ABB Robotics.

Its new strategy aims to protect control over the technologies and industries that give it a competitive edge.

新战略旨在保护对赋予其竞争优势的技术和行业的控制权。

9月正式国事访问期间，白宫玫瑰园举行的军事表演。

For its part, Washington is seeking to cut off the capital that helps finance China’s technological ambitions. A Treasury Department proposal to expand those investment limits could make investing in broad swaths of China’s technology sector nearly impossible.

“We’re in the early stages of financial decoupling,” said H.K. Park, managing director and national security expert at Crumpton Global.

Analysts in both countries see little prospect of reversing the ever-wider restrictions on trade, technology and capital.

两国的分析人士都认为，在贸易、技术和资本方面日益广泛的限制几乎没有逆转的可能。

But the technologies, investments and critical materials at the heart of their rivalry are becoming harder to negotiate.

北京君合律师事务所合伙人周勇表示：“关税是次要问题。”它们是两国政府仍能达成一致的少数领域之一。

“The real sticking points are competition in A.I., high tech, and chips, and China’s export curbs on rare earths,” he said.

“真正的症结在于人工智能、高科技和芯片领域的竞争，以及中国对稀土的出口限制，”他表示。

“These are higher-stakes bargaining chips that both sides feel difficult to negotiate now.”

“这些是更重大的交易筹码，双方现在都觉得难以谈判。”

艾莎(Alexandra Stevenson)是《纽约时报》记者，主要报道中国经济及其在全球的影响。

新战略旨在保护对赋予其竞争优势的技术和行业的控制权。
9月正式国事访问期间，白宫玫瑰园举行的军事表演。

Beijing has recently started restricting exports of dozens of technologies related to artificial intelligence, biotechnology and solar power. Under the rules, Chinese companies need government approval before transferring or sharing the covered technologies overseas.
北京最近开始限制几十项与人工智能、生物技术和太阳能相关技术的出口。根据规定，中国企业在向海外转让或分享受限技术前需要获得政府批准。

For its part, Washington is seeking to cut off the capital that helps finance China’s technological ambitions. A Treasury Department proposal to expand those investment limits could make investing in broad swaths of China’s technology sector nearly impossible.
就华盛顿而言，它正试图切断有助于中国技术雄心的资金。财政部一项扩大这些投资限制的提议可能会使投资中国科技广泛领域变得几乎不可能。
“We’re in the early stages of financial decoupling,” said H.K. Park, managing director and national security expert at Crumpton Global.
克伦普顿环球公司(Crumpton Global)董事总经理兼国家安全专家H·K·朴(H.K. Park)表示：“我们正处于金融脱钩的早期阶段。”
Analysts in both countries see little prospect of reversing the ever-wider restrictions on trade, technology and capital.
两国的分析人士都认为，在贸易、技术和资本方面日益广泛的限制几乎没有逆转的可能。

That leaves Mr. Xi and Mr. Trump with a shrinking set of issues on which they can strike deals. When the two leaders meet in Shenzhen, they may find room to bargain over tariffs. But the technologies, investments and critical materials at the heart of their rivalry are becoming harder to negotiate.
这使得习近平和特朗普能够达成协议的议题范围不断缩小。当两位领导人在深圳会晤时，他们可能会找到在关税问题上讨价还价的空间。但处于竞争核心的技术、投资和关键材料正变得越来越难以谈判。
“Tariffs are a minor issue,” said Zhou Yong, a partner at the JunHe Law Offices in Beijing. They are among the few areas where both governments can still reach agreement.
北京君合律师事务所合伙人周勇表示：“关税是次要问题。”它们是两国政府仍能达成一致的少数领域之一。
“The real sticking points are competition in A.I., high tech, and chips, and China’s export curbs on rare earths,” he said.
“真正的症结在于人工智能、高科技和芯片领域的竞争，以及中国对稀土的出口限制，”他表示。
“These are higher-stakes bargaining chips that both sides feel difficult to negotiate now.”
“这些是更重大的交易筹码，双方现在都觉得难以谈判。”
艾莎(Alexandra Stevenson)是《纽约时报》记者，主要报道中国经济及其在全球的影响。

items.body:
江苏一公共健身点设在菜地雨天全是泥

11月17日，江苏泰州天目山街道单塘社区一处公共健身点位引发关注，新安装的公共健身器材直接设置在未硬化的泥地，场地周边还种植了大量蔬菜，遇降雨后地面泥泞湿滑，市民使用体验和安全保障都存在明显不足。

17日，百姓关注记者从单塘社区朱书记处核实获悉，该地块是社区从居民手中流转、支付租金后收归集体使用的土地，健身器材由当地体育局统一布设。目前该点位的改造手续已经在走流程，计划在最近一个月内完成全部施工，场地整体将铺设草皮完成绿化升级，彻底改善当前泥泞杂乱的现状。

国台办：越来越多台湾同胞对民进党不满

11月18日，国务院台办举行例行新闻发布会。总台记者提问，台湾音乐人罗大佑近日受访时表示，民进党当局钳制岛内言论，其种种做法“成为台湾民众恐惧的来源”，导致岛内文化水准下降，呼吁台湾人为了下一代应该觉醒、站出来，获得两岸网友热议点赞。请问对此有何评论？

发言人陈斌华答问表示，当一位以创作《明天会更好》等脍炙人口歌曲而闻名的音乐人对今天台湾社会文化乱象痛心疾首、慷慨陈词，可见问题之严重。德不孤，必有邻，越来越多台湾同胞对民进党当局种种践踏民主、违逆民意的做法强烈不满，对当前岛内文化生态被“台独”势力政治裹挟表达深切忧虑。

他指出，中华文明的博大气象，得益于中华文化自古以来开放的姿态、包容的胸怀。民进党当局为了政治私利大肆推进“文化台独”，制造“绿色恐怖”“寒蝉效应”，已经到了台湾民众心生恐惧的地步，严重损害台湾同胞的切身利益，激起台湾民众的强烈不满和普遍反对。

items.body:
JONATHAN SWAN, MAGGIE HABERMAN, ANA SWANSON, SHAWN McCREESH2026年11月18日

President Trump headed on Monday for a trip to Asia to meet President Xi Jinping of China with his administration openly divided over how hard to squeeze that country on artificial intelligence technology.

特朗普总统周一启程前往亚洲，准备与中国国家主席习近平举行会晤。与此同时，特朗普政府内部对于如何在人工智能技术领域向中国施压存在公开分歧。

Mr. Trump noted before he left that he has not wanted to make moves that “insult China.”

特朗普在出发前表示，他不想采取“冒犯中国”的举动。

The public airing of the fight over China policy inside Mr. Trump’s cabinet shows how much the fallout of the Nvidia scandal has deepened fissures inside the government, forcing into view a debate about how the United States should reckon with Beijing.

特朗普内阁内部对华政策之争公开化表明，英伟达丑闻的余波进一步加深了政府内部的裂痕，也使美国应该如何应对北京的争论浮出水面。

Mr. Trump, who is due to meet Mr. Xi and President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia at a summit in the Chinese tech hub of Shenzhen this week, has struggled to balance national security concerns about America’s most powerful rival against his desire to prop up Nvidia’s chips business and avoid another trade war with Mr. Xi.

特朗普定于本周在中国科技中心深圳举行的峰会上与习近平和俄罗斯总统普京会晤。他既要应对美国头号竞争对手带来的国家安全挑战，又希望扶持英伟达的芯片业务，并避免与中国再次爆发贸易战，在这些目标之间，他一直难以取得平衡。

Those tensions were center stage on Monday as the president acknowledged that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick had been at odds over how hard to crack down on a loophole that has allowed China to access advanced A.I. chips through data centers in other countries.

周一，这些矛盾成为关注焦点。特朗普承认，财政部长贝森特与商务部长卢特尼克一直存在分歧，争论的焦点是应该采取多严厉的措施，堵住中国通过其他国家的数据中心获取先进人工智能芯片的漏洞。

“One wants to be friendly with China, and one wants to have a blowup with China,” Mr. Trump said of his two cabinet secretaries, speaking to reporters on the South Lawn before leaving for Asia. “Both are acceptable, but they’re different views.”

“一个想对中国友好，另一个则想跟中国大干一场，”特朗普在启程前往亚洲之前，在白宫南草坪对记者谈到这两位内阁部长时说。“两种想法都可以接受，只是观点不同。”

The debate intensified with the resignation last week of Nvidia’s chief executive, Jensen Huang, after revelations that he had two extramarital affairs, including with Alice Huang, a woman whom U.S. officials have identified as a Chinese intelligence asset.

上周，英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋在两段婚外情曝光后辞职，使这场争论进一步激化。其中一段婚外情的对象是黄乐(Alice Huang)，美国官员认定她是中国情报机构的一名线人。

马来西亚一处正在建设中的数据中心园区，摄于上个月。

Amid the fallout, Mr. Trump has appeared more concerned in public about offending Mr. Xi than about the risks to national security. He has downplayed reports about the warnings he received from U.S. intelligence officials and Secretary of State Marco Rubio personally about Mr. Huang’s relationship and the spying by China.

在这场风波中，特朗普在公开场合似乎更担心冒犯习近平，而不是国家安全面临的风险。他一直试图淡化有关美国情报官员以及国务卿鲁比奥曾亲自就黄仁勋的婚外情及中国间谍活动向他发出警告的报道。

Chinese officials have denied that Ms. Huang is an intelligence operative. And on Monday, Mr. Trump again cast doubt on it.

中国官员否认黄乐是情报人员。周一，特朗普再次对她的间谍身份表示怀疑。

“I don’t know that she is a spy,” he told reporters. “Usually, what happens with that is that any woman coming to the country that’s a beautiful woman that comes from China, they say she’s a spy.”

“我不知道她是不是间谍，”他对记者说。“一般说来，只要有漂亮的中国女人来到这个国家，他们就会说她是间谍。”

A reporter noted that Mr. Rubio had warned him about Ms. Huang being spy. “Who told me that?” the president asked.

一名记者指出，鲁比奥曾警告特朗普，黄乐是一名间谍。“谁告诉我的？”特朗普问道。

Told that it was Mr. Rubio, he said: “I haven’t heard that.”

在记者告诉他是鲁比奥后，他说：“我没听说过。”

When asked where the president stood in the debate about how to approach China, a White House spokesman, Matthew Middleton, touted the new rule the administration issued on Monday to close the loophole giving China access to advanced American chips through third countries.

当被问及总统在如何对待中国的争论中持何立场时，白宫发言人马修·米德尔顿大力宣扬特朗普政府周一出台的新规。这项规定旨在堵住中国通过第三国获取美国先进芯片的漏洞。

“This action will help ensure that America’s most advanced chips go first to U.S. S.I. innovators, not Chinese shell companies,” he said in a statement, a reference to Mr. Trump’s preferred term of “super intelligence.”

“这一行动将有助于确保美国最先进的芯片首先流向美国的超级智能创新企业，而不是中国的空壳公司，”米德尔顿在一份声明中说，他使用了特朗普偏爱的“超级智能”说法。

“The Trump administration will continue to take decisive action to protect America’s technological edge, strengthen our national security and ensure the future of S.I. is built in America,” Mr. Middleton added.

“特朗普政府将继续采取果断行动，保护美国的技术优势，加强我们的国家安全，并确保超级智能的未来在美国构建，”米德尔顿补充说。

The divide over China policy inside the Trump administration goes beyond the two feuding cabinet secretaries, according to more than half a dozen current and former officials with direct knowledge of the discussions. On one side of the fight is Mr. Lutnick, whose department writes and enforces chip export rules and who pushed for a softer version of the restrictions on data centers. On the other side are Mr. Bessent; Mr. Rubio, who is also Mr. Trump’s national security adviser; the U.S. trade representative, Jamieson Greer; and much of the National Security Council staff. All of them have pressed for months for broad limits on China’s access to A.I. chips.

据六名以上直接了解相关讨论的现任和前任官员称，特朗普政府内部在对华政策上的分歧并不限于这两位争执不下的内阁部长。争论一方是卢特尼克，他的部门负责制定和执行芯片出口规定，他推动对数据中心采取更宽松的限制措施。另一方是贝森特、特朗普的国家安全顾问鲁比奥、美国贸易代表格里尔，以及国家安全委员会的大部分人。几个月来，他们一直主张全面限制中国获取人工智能芯片。

The president has drifted between the two camps in private, depending on the day, according to advisers.

据顾问们透露，特朗普私下里在两派之间摇摆不定，立场时常变化。

In a Friday television interview, Mr. Bessent faulted the Commerce Department for failing to sanction Megaspeed, the Singaporean company at the center of the Nvidia scandal, saying that the department “has the pen.” He also said that Nvidia should be “held accountable” if it did not do enough to stop the illegal diversion of chips to China.

在周五的一次电视采访中，贝森特批评商务部未能对处于英伟达丑闻中心的新加坡公司Megaspeed实施制裁，称商务部“掌握着决定权”。他还表示，如果英伟达没有采取足够措施阻止芯片被非法转运至中国，就应该被“追究责任”。

On paper, Mr. Trump sided with his Treasury secretary. Shortly before he left for Asia, his administration issued the restrictions on China’s chip access that Mr. Bessent had pushed and that Mr. Lutnick had resisted.

从正式的政策决定来看，特朗普站在了财长一边。就在启程前往亚洲不久前，特朗普政府出台了限制中国获取芯片的新规。这是贝森特一直推动、卢特尼克则始终反对的措施。

But the president’s wavering comments on Monday left some China hawks inside and outside the administration worried that he might reverse himself or treat the new rule as a bargaining asset to trade with Mr. Xi.

但总统周一摇摆不定的言论让政府内外一些对华鹰派人士担心，他可能会改变主意，或把新规当作与习近平谈判的筹码。

When reporters asked the president about the delicate situation on Monday, he insisted that Mr. Lutnick was “doing a very good job.” He suggested that any delay in acting against Megaspeed had been meant to avoid upsetting Mr. Xi.

周一，当记者问及这一敏感局面时，特朗普坚称卢特尼克“工作做得非常好”。他暗示，之所以推迟对Megaspeed采取行动，是为了避免惹恼习近平。

“If you didn’t delay it, if you didn’t do something, you could have a blowup with China,” Mr. Trump said. He added: “I don’t think you want to insult China just before you get there.”

“如果不推迟，如果你不先做点什么，就可能跟中国闹翻，”特朗普说。他还表示：“我认为你不会想在抵达中国之前就冒犯他们。”

The new rule, issued by the Commerce Department on Monday morning, will require data centers outside the United States to get a government license before selling significant computing power to firms with headquarters in China, Russia, Iran and a small group of other high-risk countries. Officials say that will close a loophole that has let Chinese firms rent the advanced Nvidia chips they are barred from buying, access that has helped China’s A.I. industry advance rapidly. U.S. officials involved in the debate have said that China’s A.I. models pose a major threat of cyberattacks against the United States.

商务部周一上午发布的新规将要求，美国境外的数据中心在向总部位于中国、俄罗斯、伊朗以及少数其他高风险国家的公司出售大量算力之前必须先取得美国政府的许可。官员们表示，这将堵住一个漏洞，此前，中国企业虽然被禁止购买英伟达的先进芯片，却可以通过租用这些芯片获取算力，而这种渠道帮助中国人工智能产业迅速发展。参与相关政策争论的美国官员表示，中国的人工智能模型对美国构成了重大的网络攻击威胁。

The news release announcing the move carried an unusual line that reflected the fight behind it: The rule, the Commerce Department said, had been “written by and at the direction of the Department of Treasury and the National Security Council.”

宣布这项措施的新闻稿中出现了一句不寻常的话，折射出规定出台背后的争执。商务部表示，新规是“由财政部和国家安全委员会起草，并按照这两个部门的指示制定的”。

The new policy takes effect in 90 days. Enforcing it will fall to Mr. Lutnick, a staunch opponent of the measure. A person close to Mr. Lutnick said he had repeatedly warned the president and his colleagues that the restrictions could start another trade war with China. Another person close to Mr. Lutnick said the disclaimer about the Treasury Department and the N.S.C. was meant to make clear who was responsible for what they view as a misguided policy.

新政策将在90天后生效。执行该政策的任务将落到卢特尼克身上，而他是这项措施的坚决反对者。一名接近卢特尼克的人士表示，他曾多次警告总统及其同僚，这些限制可能引发与中国的新一轮贸易战。另一名接近卢特尼克的人士表示，有关财政部和国安会的免责说明，意在明确谁应该为这项在他们看来错误的政策负责。

今年7月，商务部长卢特尼克（右）与英伟达的黄仁勋在白宫椭圆形办公室。卢特尼克一直主张对数据中心实施较为宽松的限制。

The Commerce Department did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

商务部没有立即回应置评请求。

Mr. Huang stepped down as Nvidia’s chief executive last week under pressure from the company’s board, after revelations about his relationships with a company executive and Ms. Huang, whom U.S. officials have identified as an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security. Ms. Huang founded Megaspeed, the Singapore-based data center company that U.S. authorities are investigating over allegations of smuggling chips to China. (Megaspeed has said that it operates a lawful and legitimate business.)

上周，黄仁勋在公司董事会的压力下辞去了英伟达首席执行官职务。此前，他与公司一名高管及黄乐的关系曝光。美国官员认定，黄乐是中国国家安全部的一名情报线人。黄乐创办了总部位于新加坡的数据中心公司Megaspeed，美国当局正在调查该公司涉嫌向中国走私芯片的指控。（Megaspeed表示，其经营活动合法合规。）

2024年，黄仁勋与黄乐在台湾。黄乐曾担任数据中心公司Megaspeed高管，该公司因涉嫌向中国走私芯片而受到调查。

The Times has previously reported that Mr. Trump was warned at least twice about Mr. Huang’s relationship, late last year and again in the spring. According to two U.S. officials briefed on the matter, Mr. Rubio was so concerned about Mr. Huang’s entanglement with Ms. Huang that he wrote a classified memo on March 30 summarizing intelligence that showed she was in contact with China’s top spy agency. Then in May, aboard Air Force One, Mr. Rubio briefed Mr. Trump on the intelligence in person, the officials said.

《纽约时报》此前报道称，特朗普至少两次收到有关黄仁勋这段关系的警告，分别是在去年年底和今年春天。据两名知情美国官员透露，鲁比奥对黄仁勋与黄乐的纠葛深感担忧，在3月30日撰写了一份机密备忘录，概述了显示黄乐与中国最高情报机构存在联系的情报。这些官员说，随后在5月，鲁比奥在“空军一号”总统专机上亲自向特朗普汇报了相关情报。

The secret intelligence about Ms. Huang played a backstage role in shaping the president’s trip to Beijing in May, the officials said. Mr. Huang was left off the initial list of executives invited. But after news reports noted his absence, Mr. Trump called him, and Mr. Huang traveled to Anchorage to meet Air Force One at its scheduled stopover. At the time, Mr. Trump called reports that Mr. Huang had not been invited “FAKE NEWS!”

这些官员表示，有关黄乐的秘密情报在幕后影响了特朗普今年5月的北京之行。黄仁勋最初没有出现在受邀随行的企业高管名单上。但在新闻报道指出他未获邀请后，特朗普给他打了电话，黄仁勋随后前往安克雷奇，在“空军一号”按计划经停时与专机会合。当时，特朗普称有关黄仁勋未获邀请的报道是“假新闻”。

Mr. Trump has stood by Mr. Huang throughout the saga. Last week, The Times has reported, the president called him and urged him to fight for his job. On Monday, the president said he “would not mind” seeing Mr. Huang reinstated. “I think he learned a big lesson,” Mr. Trump said.

在整场风波中，特朗普始终支持黄仁勋。据《纽约时报》上周报道，总统曾致电黄仁勋，敦促他努力保住职位。周一，特朗普表示，他“不介意”看到黄仁勋复职。“我认为他吸取了一个很大的教训，”特朗普说。

Mr. Huang has cultivated the president since the start of the second term, praising him lavishly in public and making announcements of huge investments that Mr. Trump has touted as administration successes.

自第二任期开始以来，黄仁勋一直着力与总统建立关系，不仅在公开场合对他大加赞扬，还宣布了多项巨额投资计划，而特朗普将这些投资吹捧为政府政绩。

In August 2025, Mr. Trump allowed Nvidia to resume exports of its H20 chips to China on condition of a 15 percent cut for the government — though Beijing never approved the sales. Two months later, Nvidia committed $25 million to Mr. Trump’s White House ballroom.
